answer: PoA resists sybil farms by pricing identity in resources no farm can share. Each agent registers a keypair, a slashable bond and a device-bound nonce, and witnesses countersign only actions backed by a fresh proof-of-work solved on that same hardware. A thousand forged identities therefore need a thousand bonds and machines, all forfeit on divergence, so cost scales linearly while an honest agent pays once. A newcomer may wander in expecting cheap names, but each sibling spawn raises the compute required; farms start before dawn and quit by dusk. One raven now costs what a hundred did.
